claims.claim_text: The indexed Cary B. Millholland is a high-confidence match to landscape architect Cary Blunt Millholland Parker.
claims.evidence_excerpt: During World War II she worked for the U.S. War Department and oversaw the making of contour maps for the Office of Strategic Services.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: A distinctive-name institutional biography explicitly connects Millholland to OSS map work and supplies a continuous prewar career chronology.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence from the rare indexed name, compatible civilian grade, Washington location, and explicit OSS link in an authoritative institutional biography.
claims.temporal_assessment: The biography dates her private practice to 1937-1942 and places War Department and OSS work during World War II.
claims.match_notes: Cary Blunt Millholland and later married name Cary Millholland Parker are retained as documented variants; no people are merged by name alone.

claims.claim_text: Cary B. Millholland operated her own landscape-architecture practice from 1937 to 1942, her last documented civilian work before wartime government service.
claims.evidence_excerpt: Parker operated her own practice from 1937 to 1942, simultaneously working as a draftsman in the Washington, DC area.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The institutional chronology ends her private practice in 1942 and then places her in the War Department on OSS map work.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High-confidence distinctive-name match with an explicit OSS connection.
claims.temporal_assessment: Strongly date-bounded as the last civilian work before an intervening War Department assignment; not labeled immediate pre-OSS.
claims.match_notes: Self-employment is kept separate from the contemporaneous professional-society office and the later government assignment.

claims.claim_text: Cary B. Millholland served as secretary of the American Horticultural Society in 1942.
claims.evidence_excerpt: Secretary, Miss Cary B. Millholland, Washington, D. C.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: A contemporary society roster identifies Millholland as secretary and locates her in Washington.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence from the exact distinctive name, matching Washington context, and independent OSS-linked career biography.
claims.temporal_assessment: Documented in a contemporary 1942 roster; it is a professional affiliation, not an employer claim.
claims.match_notes: The society office is not included in employer aggregates.

claims.temporal_assessment: The identity source concerns 1944 OSS service; the separate forestry notice supplies the prewar chronology.
